lane: LANE B1 — projectiles do not read as projectiles (archer arrow / bat-rider harpoon; fiery-vs-plain by target class)
owner_item: "Archers don't really show to be firing arrows now — or sometimes they do, but they don't fly. All the arrows, either archers or the bat riders, anyone who's shooting should be more coherent and look [right]. The bat riders, they're throwing harpoons, so it should look like a harpoon, a FIERY harpoon at TOWERS and a REGULAR harpoon at CREATURES. Same with the archers — regular arrows at creatures and FIERY arrows at buildings. But it is not like that, so we need that fixed."
root_cause:
THERE IS A TRAVELLING PROJECTILE SYSTEM AND IT IS ALREADY DERIVED — SO THIS LANE IS "FIX THE VISUAL", NOT "BUILD A PROJECTILE". `src/render/creatureProjectile.ts` (S153 P2 / S154 P2) resolves a flying arrow (goblinArcher) and harpoon (goblinBat) every frame from synced state, interpolating the tip along `from`→`to` by `t`, with a flaming/plain split. It is wired and called (`goblinRenderer.ts:882`). Nothing needs inventing.

⛔ **DEFECT 1 — THE PRIMARY ONE, AND IT IS A SILENT S181 REGRESSION. The renderer only knows how to aim at a SHAPE, and since S181 a unit attacking a building aims at a CONNECTOR instead — so NO arrow is drawn at all, and the FIERY branch is now effectively dead against every actual building.**

The victim resolution is exactly two arms (`creatureProjectile.ts:107-140`): an enemy *creature* inside `attackRange` (→ plain), else `c.targetPrimitiveId` (→ flaming). If both miss it returns `null` and draws nothing.

S181's targeting rework made that second arm almost never hold. `structureTargets` (`creatureAI.ts:203-228`) returns **exactly one** of `{primitiveId, bondId}` — its own comment says so — and `findNearestEnemyPrimitiveFrom` **skips any shape that has a connector** (`creatureAI.ts:267`, S179's "a building is killed through its connectors, not by eating its bricks"). So against a standing tower the host sets `targetBondId` and **`targetPrimitiveId = null`** (`hostTick.ts:1577-1578`). The renderer consults only `targetPrimitiveId`. Result: shooting a tower draws nothing.

The same hole exists for every other strike arm the sim has and the renderer does not: the **castle** (`creatureAttack.ts` castle arm, derived from position — no bond, no primitive), a **defender** (`creatureAttack.ts:307` — Helga / laser turret / stink tower live in `world.defenders`, and the renderer's loop walks `world.creatures` only), and a **landed stink bag** (`creatureAttack.ts:435`). Five of the sim's six strike arms draw no projectile.

⭐ THIS IS EXACTLY HIS SENTENCE. *"Sometimes they do"* = an enemy unit is inside range (plain arrow — the one arm that still works), or a genuinely loose brick is nearer (fiery arrow — at the ONE thing that is not a building). *"Archers don't really show to be firing arrows"* = every shot at a tower, a castle, a turret or Helga.

⛔ **DEFECT 2 — THE FLIGHT IS 12 TICKS AND A NETWORKED PEER SAMPLES IT TWICE.** `ARROW_FLIGHT_TICKS = 12` (`constants.ts:3785`), ending on `attackFireTick` 30. On host/solo the sim runs at `PHYSICS_HZ = 60` so `t` advances every render frame — it does fly, for 0.2 s. On a **client** `ticksInState` is non-position state, snapped once per snapshot in `needsFullApply` and **never interpolated** — `sync.ts:301-308` says in as many words "Positions only — non-position state was snapped to the LATEST snapshot". At `NET_SNAPSHOT_HZ = 10` (`constants.ts:912`) that is a 6-tick jump, so the 13-tick-wide window yields 2–3 discrete positions, each held ~6 render frames. A joiner sees two stamped sticks, not flight.

⛔ **DEFECT 3 — EVEN ON THE HOST IT STROBES.** The shaft is 13 px (`SHAFT_LEN`, `creatureProjectile.ts:157`). Over the archer's 220 px reach in 12 frames the tip advances ~18 px/frame — further than the arrow is long, so consecutive frames do not overlap and it reads as a dashed flicker rather than a moving object. Compare `CASTLE_SHOT_VFX_TICKS = 24` (`raceMotifs.ts:52`) for the same journey, and `DEFENDER_FIRE_HOLD_TICKS = 12` whose comment says a fire window is sized to span "≥2 snapshot intervals" — 12 is the floor for *being seen at all*, not for reading as flight.

⚠ DEFECT 4 (pre-existing, already named in the file at `creatureProjectile.ts:116-122`) — when several enemies are in range the renderer picks the **lowest id** while the sim strikes the one `pickNavUnit` chose (nearest). The arrow can lean at the wrong unit. Cosmetic; worth closing while the function is open.

⛔ NON-FINDING, CHECKED AND RULED BENIGN SO NOBODY RE-RAISES IT: `syncCreatureProjectiles` has no `isConcealed` gate where the sprite loop does (`goblinRenderer.ts:919`), which looks like a fog leak. It is not reachable — `fogActive` is `isNetworked && PLAYING && matchPhase === 'BUILD'` (`vision.ts:174-176`) and creatures fight in FIGHT. Do not "fix" it.

evidence.why_it_matters: THE WHOLE BUG IN ONE LINE. The only structure the renderer can aim at is a PRIMITIVE. Since S181 a unit attacking a building commits to a BOND and this field is null, so the fiery branch never runs against a real tower.
And when it is null the function draws NOTHING. That is 'archers don't really show to be firing arrows' — not a wrong-looking arrow, an absent one.

evidence.quote: * ⛔ EXACTLY ONE OF THE TWO IS RETURNED. Setting both would put the creature into ATTACKING
evidence.why_it_matters: structureTargets is mutually exclusive by design. `primitiveId` and `bondId` are never both set, so 'read targetPrimitiveId' is the same as 'ignore every building'.

S179's lone-shape rule. Any shape inside a structure is skipped, so targetPrimitiveId only ever holds a LOOSE brick or a stink bag — the one class of target that is NOT a building, which is precisely where the flaming arrow does fire today.
With the line below it (`creature.targetBondId = st.bondId;`) this is the host writing null into the one field the renderer reads, every time a unit picks a standing building.
THE FIX IS FREE. targetBondId is emitted on the wire, additive-optional. No new field, no PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.

And it is rehydrated on the CLIENT. trimMirrorCreature (save.ts:1447) strips only targetCreatureId, so a joiner can read the bond and compute bondMidpoint locally — the derived design holds with zero wire cost.

fix_shape:
**ALL THREE FIXES LIVE IN ONE FILE, `src/render/creatureProjectile.ts`. Render-only. No wire field, no bump, no art.**

── 1 · TEACH THE RESOLVER THE OTHER FIVE TARGET CLASSES (the fix he is actually asking for)

Replace the two-arm resolution at `creatureProjectile.ts:101-140` with arms that MIRROR the sim's strike order in `creatureAttack.ts` (creature → defender → primitive → stink cloud → bond → castle), each returning `{to, flaming}`:

| arm | `to` from | on the wire? | flaming |
|---|---|---|---|
| enemy creature in `attackRange` | `other.pos` | yes (`world.creatures`) | **false** — plain |
| enemy defender in reach | `d.pos` (`world.defenders`) | yes | `kind === 'princess'` → **false** (Helga is a unit-class defender, canon §4); `turret` / `stinkTower` → **true** |
| `c.targetPrimitiveId` | `prim.pos` | yes (`save.ts:2121`) | **true** |
| enemy stink cloud in reach | cloud pos | yes | **true** (it is a placed lone shape, canon §2) |
| **`c.targetBondId`** ← THE MISSING ONE | **`bondMidpoint(world.bonds.get(id))`**, already exported at `creatureAI.ts:79` and reading live primitive bodies both peers hold | **yes — `save.ts:2120` emits, `:2484` rehydrates, `trimMirrorCreature` (`:1447`) strips only `targetCreatureId`** | **true** — this is a tower |
| enemy castle in reach | `castleAnchor(seat, world.layout)` | yes (`world.players`, `world.layout`) | **true** (needs his ruling — see below) |

⛔ THE ORDER IS THE CONTRACT, NOT A PREFERENCE. Today the renderer prefers *any* creature in range over the committed shape; the sim's shape arm can fall through (`creatureAttack.ts:352-403`, S178) while the creature arm cannot. Matching the order is what stops the picture contradicting the hit — which is the stated reason the flight window ends on `attackFireTick` in the first place.

⭐ AND CLOSE THE LOWEST-ID DIVERGENCE WHILE THE FUNCTION IS OPEN. Swap the `bestId`/lowest-id scan (`:126-130`) for nearest-then-lower-id, matching `pickNavUnit`. It is a two-line change inside code already being rewritten; leaving it is how the *next* session reports "the arrow points at the wrong goblin".

── 2 · MAKE IT FLY ON A JOINER (this is `sync.ts`'s constraint, not a bug in this file)

`ticksInState` steps 6 at a time on a client. Two options; **take (a), it is smaller and it is already precedent**:

**(a) Widen the window to 24 and streak the shaft.** Set `ARROW_FLIGHT_TICKS = 24` — start becomes `30 − 24 = 6`, still inside `[0, attackFireTick]`, still landing exactly on the fire tick. That is 0.4 s, matching `CASTLE_SHOT_VFX_TICKS` for the same journey, and gives a client 4–5 samples instead of 2. Then draw the shaft as a MOTION STREAK: extend the tail backward along the flight axis by the per-frame step (~9 px at 24 ticks) with a falling alpha, so successive positions overlap instead of leaving gaps. Both changes are pure arithmetic in the existing draw functions.

**(b) (do NOT take unless he asks) Sub-tick smoothing from a render clock.** `turretRenderer.ts:171` and `stinkTowerRenderer` already use `performance.now()` for render-only cosmetics, so the precedent exists — but it makes the two peers' *pictures* differ mid-flight for no gain he asked for, and it adds a clock to a function whose whole documented virtue is being a pure function of synced state.

── 3 · KEEP THE SILHOUETTES, FIX WHAT THEY MEAN

`PROJECTILE_BY_TYPE` (`:78-81`) already maps `goblinArcher → 'arrow'`, `goblinBat → 'harpoon'`, and `drawHarpoon` (`:243-290`) already gives the harpoon a heavier 2.6 shaft, swept barbs and a trailing hemp line — exactly what he asked a harpoon to look like. **Do not redesign the art.** Once arm 5 above exists, "fiery harpoon at towers, regular harpoon at creatures" is satisfied by the `flaming` flag the draw functions already branch on.

⚠ ONE REAL LOOK-BUG TO FIX WHILE THERE: a flaming arrow drops its fletching (`:220-227`) AND recolours the shaft to `FLAME_CORE`, so at 13 px a burning arrow is a bright line with a blob — the harpoon/arrow distinction disappears the moment either burns. Keep the plain shaft colour under the flame wake so the SILHOUETTE still identifies the shooter when it is on fire. That is the "more coherent" half of his sentence.

── OUT OF SCOPE, NAMED SO IT IS NOT SILENTLY DROPPED
The stink tower's static lob arc (`stinkTowerRenderer.ts:265`) is the same defect class in a second file — the bag does not travel, the whole parabola is drawn every frame and a splash ring sits on the target. `d.lastStrikePos` and `d.ticksInState` are both synced, so the same `t`-interpolation would fix it in ~10 lines. **It is a DIFFERENT file and a different owner complaint — give it its own branch or its own priority, do not let it widen this one** (S182 §5: scope of change drives the defect rate).
determinism_risk:
NONE-RENDER-ONLY, and the reason is structural rather than a promise.

- `creatureProjectile.ts` is imported by `goblinRenderer.ts` and by tests, and by nothing in `src/state/` — it cannot reach the sim. Verified: the only non-test importer is `goblinRenderer.ts:37`.
- **NO PROTOCOL_VERSION BUMP. 47 STANDS.** Every field the new arms read already rides the wire: `targetBondId` emitted `save.ts:2120` / rehydrated `:2484` / NOT stripped (`trimMirrorCreature`, `:1447`, strips `targetCreatureId` alone); `targetPrimitiveId` `:2121`; `world.bonds`, `world.defenders`, `world.players`, `world.layout` all synced. **No new `GameEffect` kind**, so none of the four exhaustive switches and no `deserializeEffect` default arm is touched. This is the derive-don't-send channel the file's own docblock (`:16-46`) exists to defend, extended — not abandoned.
- **NO four-sites obligation** (factory / serialize / hash / worker): nothing is added to a hashed entity. `hashWorldState` and `hashWorldStateFull` are untouched.
- The resolver stays a pure function of synced state with a total order (nearest, then lower id), so host and joiner still compute the same picture. ⚠ A divergence here would be COSMETIC ONLY — it is never hashed and never read by the sim — but keeping the total order is what stops a "looks like desync" bug report.
- ⚠ THE ONE REAL RISK, AND IT IS THE PARALLEL-SPLIT RISK, NOT A SIM RISK: `src/constants.ts` is a magnet file. `ARROW_FLIGHT_TICKS` is a one-line edit at `constants.ts:3785`; if any sibling branch is also in `constants.ts`, that is the S182 §3 hazard (a defect between two branches has no owner). The merge owner should take this branch alone or last, and re-run the suite between merges.
art_cost:
**NO-ART. ZERO SPEND. THE NO-COST PATH IS THE ONLY PATH HERE, AND IT IS ALREADY BUILT.**

Both projectiles are drawn **procedurally in Pixi `Graphics`** and always have been — no sprite, no atlas, no texture, no tint of an existing sheet, nothing to generate:
- the arrow: a stroked shaft, a filled triangle head, two fletching strokes (`creatureProjectile.ts:206-227`);
- the harpoon: a heavier stroked shaft, a filled spike-plus-barbs polygon, a `quadraticCurveTo` slack line (`:258-289`);
- the fire: three stacked translucent circles trailing the tip (`:193-203`, `:266-276`).

The file states the reason itself at `:172-175`: *"two new textures would count against the texture-census growth budget the repo tracks, and a procedural flame costs none of it while reading correctly at this size."*

⭐ SO THE ANSWER TO HIS MONEY RULE IS UNCONDITIONAL: **a fiery arrow and a fiery harpoon already exist and cost nothing; they are simply never drawn at a building.** The work is to fix which target they aim at, not to make a picture. Widening the flight window and adding the motion streak are also pure arithmetic — no asset, no `check:atlas` run, no `ART_PIPELINE.md` stage 1-5 round, no veo clip (~$20 each, his own measurement). **If anyone proposes generating arrow/harpoon sprites for this lane, that is a strictly worse and strictly more expensive version of what is already shipped.** Do not do it.
tests_owed:
⚠ NO RENDERER RUNS UNDER VITEST — Helga drew on top of her own hall with the whole suite green. So be precise about the split.

**WHAT CAN BE PINNED HARD, AND IT IS THE ENTIRE BUG.** `resolveProjectileShot` is a PURE function over `(World, Creature)` and is already unit-tested (`creatureProjectile.test.ts` imports it directly). The defect is a `null` return and a wrong `flaming` flag — both fully assertable with no GPU. Owed:

1. ⛔ **THE REGRESSION TEST THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THIS.** Build a world with a bonded enemy structure and NO loose shape, put an archer in ATTACKING mid-window with `targetBondId` set and `targetPrimitiveId = null` (the exact state `hostTick.ts:1577-1578` writes), assert `shot !== null` **and** `shot.flaming === true` **and** `shot.to` equals `bondMidpoint`. Repeat for `goblinBat`. **Today every structure case in that file sets `targetPrimitiveId` and not one sets `targetBondId` — that omission is the whole reason a green suite shipped this.**
2. One case per new arm — defender (turret → flaming, Helga → plain), castle, stink cloud — each asserting `flaming` as well as non-null.
3. ⭐ **A MECHANICAL ARM-COUNT GUARD, the S182 §2 pattern with teeth.** A source-text tripwire asserting "this predicate is wired" would be green over exactly this bug, because the failing path never consulted the predicate. Instead COUNT: enumerate the sim's strike arms in `creatureAttack.ts` and pin the resolver's arm count equal to it, naming each pair. A seventh strike arm then turns this test RED until someone decides what it throws. State the limit on itself: it proves the arms EXIST and are counted, not that each aims correctly — (1) and (2) are what prove that.
4. Ordering test: with a creature in range AND a bond committed, assert the creature wins (mirrors `creatureAttack.ts`'s arm order); and nearest-not-lowest-id with two enemies at different distances.
5. `ARROW_FLIGHT_TICKS`: if it moves to 24, assert `attackFireTick - ARROW_FLIGHT_TICKS >= 0` for every type in `PROJECTILE_BY_TYPE`, derived from the constants — never a literal. And re-check the two existing window-boundary tests, which are written against 12.

⚠ **BLAST RADIUS TO RE-RUN, NOT ONLY THE OWNED TESTS.** `src/state/untargetableRetention.test.ts:314` asserts `resolveProjectileShot` returns **null** for an archer with no valid unit and no committed shape. Adding bond/castle/defender arms can flip that fixture to non-null depending on what its world contains. Read it and re-pin it deliberately — do not relax the assertion to make it pass (canon: re-pin, never silence).

**WHAT CANNOT BE PINNED, STATED HONESTLY.** No test in this repo can see that the arrow is *drawn*, that it *reads* as an arrow rather than a harpoon, that the flame does not swallow the silhouette, that the streak overlaps frame-to-frame, or that a joiner perceives flight rather than two stamps. `drawArrow`/`drawHarpoon`/`drawProjectile` are deliberately untested and the test file says why (`creatureProjectile.test.ts:9-11`). Those are owner-eyes questions. A Playwright `@races`-style observation could in principle catch "nothing drawn at a tower" via a pixel probe, but each observation costs ~30 s of SIM time and that lane is separately CI-gated — **propose it only if the owner asks; the pure-function tests above already pin the defect itself.**
owner_ruling_needed: THE CASTLE — fiery or plain? A keep is a building, so the rule says fiery, and that is the sensible default to SHIP unless he objects. Flagged only because the castle is the one deliberate exception elsewhere in the canon (§3, CASTLE_MAX_HP off the pool ladder) and he has a habit of treating it as its own thing. Build it fiery, name it in the commit, one line reverses it.

HELGA — plain or fiery? Canon §4 calls her 'a unit-class defender' and she is a person, so PLAIN is the reading of his own words ('regular arrows at creatures'). But she is reached through world.defenders alongside the laser turret and the stink tower, which are unambiguously buildings and get fiery. Default to plain, pin it in a test, tell him the one-line lever.

⭐ THE ONE THING WORTH HIS BREATH, ASKED AS A NUMBER RATHER THAN A DESIGN QUESTION: does he want the arrow visibly SLOWER? Today it crosses the archer's full 220 px reach in 0.2 s and lands exactly on the damage tick. Doubling the window to 0.4 s (matching the castle bolt) is what makes it read as flight on a joiner, and the ONLY cost is that the arrow leaves the bow 0.2 s earlier in the wind-up — the hit still lands on the same tick, so no balance changes. Show him the two numbers, not the mechanism.
size_estimate:
STANDARD — about half a session, one branch, one production file.

~90-140 lines rewritten inside `src/render/creatureProjectile.ts` (six victim arms replacing two, nearest-then-id ordering, the motion streak, the flaming-silhouette fix), one constant line in `src/constants.ts`, ~150 lines of new tests plus a re-pin in `untargetableRetention.test.ts`. No new file, no new module, no atlas, no wire change, no PROTOCOL_VERSION bump.

⛔ **SAY "FIX ONLY THIS" IN THE BRIEF** (S182 §5 — the defect rate tracked how much each session changed, not how hard the task was). Specifically DO NOT let this branch drift into: the stink tower's static lob arc (different file, own priority), the laser beam (correct as a laser), boss ability VFX, or `ARROW_FLIGHT_TICKS`-adjacent retunes of the attack cadence. The file boundary is `src/render/creatureProjectile.ts` plus its tests plus one constant.

⚠ FILE-COLLISION WARNING FOR THE MERGE OWNER: `src/constants.ts` is the only shared-magnet file here. If a sibling branch also edits it, merge this one alone and re-run `npx vitest run` before the next merge — two branches that are each green can be red together.

Gates before hand-back: `npm run typecheck`, `npx vitest run`, `npm run build` (bundle charter — 852.2 KiB of 1000 measured S182; this adds no asset so headroom is untouched). **Read each exit code DIRECTLY, never through a pipe, and never trust the wrapper's trailing `[exited with code 0]`** — redirect to a file and echo `$?`. `npm run e2e:gating` only if the merge owner re-runs it on the merged tree; no branch's e2e number is trustworthy on its own.
blocked_on: NOTHING. Every question this lane asked is answered in code, the fix needs no owner input to start, and the two rulings above have safe defaults that can ship and be reversed with one line each. Work was READ-ONLY throughout — no file in the tree was created, edited or deleted, and no npm/vitest/build command was run.
